latestUpstreamCheck.conclusion: The official registry still lists 4.0.7 as latest and no 4.0.8 package. The GitHub advisory has no first_patched_version. The local patch is not represented as an upstream release.
latestUpstreamCheck.upstreamTests: The exact official git tree contains 37 JavaScript test files. The npm distribution omits these tests. The upstream full test suite was not executed or claimed to pass.

algorithm: Inspect the compiled body of repeated plus/star extglobs for variable repetition, optional quantifiers, ranges, backreferences and nested alternatives while respecting escapes and character classes.

For a single-segment P*Q body containing one wildcard star plus ordinary filename literals and bounded one-character wildcards, remove the surrounding unbounded repetition. Concatenating any two accepted segments is still accepted by that body.

Allow a union of these bodies when all branches share the prefix or all share the suffix; always retain a noncapturing group around the entire union. Outer star is represented by an optional body to preserve its zero repetitions.
Reuse the compiled body so existing platform separator and dot rules remain in effect. Keep existing upstream repeated-extglob safeguards and safe reductions.

If the new variable-length form cannot be normalized under these conditions, throw SyntaxError with PICOMATCH_UNSAFE_REPEAT during compilation. The new guard remains active even when maxExtglobRecursion is false.
compatibilityBoundaries: This is a conservative defensive repair, not a claim that every valid extglob retains its previous result. Some complex or nested variable-length forms are explicitly rejected instead of silently producing a different matcher.

Capture-enabled and bash-mode variable repeated forms are rejected rather than incorrectly preserving last-iteration capture or cross-separator semantics. Ordinary finite extglobs and ordinary capture/bash matching remain available.

Common same-prefix or same-suffix multi-branch filename patterns remain supported. Arbitrary differing-prefix-and-suffix branches, path-crossing bodies and nested alternatives outside the proven normalization are not newly supported.
Compiled-structure and bounded ordinary-filename checks support the chosen fix. They do not prove universal regex complexity or all upstream option combinations.

validation.constraints: No denial-of-service input, exploit reproduction, long-string test, timing threshold or live external service was created or executed. Unsupported patterns were compiled only; matching used fixed ordinary filenames at most 24 characters in the comparison and 32 in committed tests.

windowsInstalledDependency.actualModuleResolution: createRequire(realpathSync(node_modules/vitest/package.json)) resolves the actual transitive installed package used by Vitest.

linuxInstalledDependency.environment: Fresh dependency tree installed offline in a task-only directory. Targeted execution used a separate network namespace with loopback only.

fullAuditAndMatrix.note: No full-suite pass or release readiness is claimed by this targeted repair report.

intermediateEvidence.outcome: Zero tests executed because createRequire was anchored at the pnpm symlink instead of its real target. Corrected to realpathSync; not used as behavioral red evidence.

The unpatched package ran 21 cases: 19 failed and 2 passed. One failure was a fixture misclassification of an escaped literal plus fixed-width wildcard; the other 18 corresponded to intended structure/rejection changes. The fixture was corrected and a positive fixed-width case added, yielding the final 22 cases. No production patch change was required for this fixture correction.

Independent review caught missing grouping around the initial multi-branch normalization. The final patch always groups the whole compiled inner source, and committed regressions cover adjacent prefix/suffix literals and one-sided nonmatches. All final evidence refers to the corrected hash.

An exploratory display used a matcher directly as Array.filter callback, whose index is interpreted as an optional diagnostic flag. That display was corrected to a one-argument callback and was not used as accepted evidence. The committed tests and the 7752-comparison checker use one-argument calls.

integrationOwnership: Workspace/lock/installation/deployment and the exact-content dependency gate are independently implemented and tested by other agents. The linked deployment report preserves its intermediate failures and proves actual offline installation/build rather than relying on copied package content.
